# ScramServerCollision

*Server*

Custom collision of a world: a solid convex shape (box, cylinder, prism, wedge, sphere) that players and other entities collide with like with blocks. Near collisions entities move like in Source engine games: they slide along walls, walk up and down slopes up to about 45 degrees, slide down steeper ones and step up obstacles up to their step height. Mobs find paths over and around collisions like over blocks.

Create it with `c.getWorld().createCollision(id)` (or `createCollision()` for a generated ID), give it a shape with [`box`](#box), [`cylinder`](#cylinder), [`prism`](#prism), [`wedge`](#wedge) or [`sphere`](#sphere), place it and call [`spawn()`](#spawn). The position is the center of the shape (or its anchor, see [`setAnchor`](#setanchor)), and the rotation turns it around that point. Changes of an added collision apply at once. An added collision can be moved, turned, resized and turned into another shape smoothly with

[`moveTo`](#moveto), [`rotateTo`](#rotateto), [`sizeTo`](#sizeto) and [`transformTo`](#transformto); by default it carries entities standing on it and pushes entities in its way, see

[`setCarrying(boolean)`](#setcarrying). Collisions are saved with the world. Entities touching, using or hitting collisions fire the "Collision: ..." events, with the collision in `c.getValue("collision")`. Shown by hitboxes (F3 + B).

```js
function main(c) {
    var pos = c.getPlayer().getPosition();

    // A ramp 4 blocks wide, rising 2 blocks over 4 blocks towards +Z
    c.getWorld().createCollision("ramp").wedge(4, 2, 4).setPosition(pos.x, pos.y + 1, pos.z + 4).spawn();
}
```

## Methods

### getId {#getid}

::: member

**Returns** [`String`](/scripting/js/String) — collision ID, unique within its world

:::

### spawn {#spawn}

::: member

Adds the collision to its world, replacing the added collision with the same ID and stopping its animations.

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### remove {#remove}

::: member

Removes the collision with this ID from its world. Does nothing if it is not added.

:::

### isAdded {#isadded}

::: member

**Returns** [`boolean`](/scripting/js/Boolean) — true if a collision with this ID is added in its world

:::

### isAnimating {#isanimating}

::: member

**Returns** [`boolean`](/scripting/js/Boolean) — true while a [`moveTo`](#moveto), [`rotateTo`](#rotateto), [`sizeTo`](#sizeto) or [`transformTo`](#transformto) of the added collision runs

:::

### box {#box}

::: member

Makes the collision a box centered on its anchor at once, see [`setShape`](#setshape).

```js
// A 3 x 1 x 3 platform
c.getWorld().createCollision("platform").box(3, 1, 3).setPosition(0, 65, 0).spawn();
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sizeX` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | size along X, positive |
| `sizeY` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | size along Y, positive |
| `sizeZ` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | size along Z, positive |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### cylinder {#cylinder}

::: member

Makes the collision a vertical cylinder with `#DEFAULT_SEGMENTS` sides at once, see

[`cylinder(double, double, int)`](#cylinder).

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `radius` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | radius, positive |
| `height` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | size along Y, positive |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### cylinder {#cylinder-2}

::: member

Makes the collision a vertical cylinder at once, see [`setShape`](#setshape). The circle is a regular polygon with its corners on the circle; more sides are rounder but cost more to collide with.

```js
c.getWorld().createCollision("pillar").cylinder(1, 4, 12).setPosition(0, 66, 0).spawn();
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `radius` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | radius, positive |
| `height` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | size along Y, positive |
| `segments` | [`int`](/scripting/js/Number) | number of sides, from 3 to 64 |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### prism {#prism}

::: member

Makes the collision a vertical prism at once, see [`setShape`](#setshape): a convex polygon extruded along Y, centered vertically. The polygon points are relative to the anchor, so rectangles, triangles, trapezoids and other convex polygons give boxes and columns of these shapes. For concave shapes add several collisions.

```js
var world = c.getWorld();

// Triangle column 2 blocks high
world.createCollision("triangle").prism([0, 0, 3, 0, 0, 3], 2).setPosition(10, 65, 10).spawn();

// Trapezoid: 4 blocks wide at the back, 2 at the front
world.createCollision("trapezoid").prism([-2, 0, 2, 0, 1, 2, -1, 2], 1).setPosition(20, 64.5, 10).spawn();
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `points` | `List<Number>` | x, z of every polygon point in order around it (either direction), like `[x1, z1, x2, z2, x3, z3]` |
| `height` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | size along Y, positive |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### wedge {#wedge}

::: member

Makes the collision a ramp at once, see [`setShape`](#setshape): its bottom fills the X and Z sizes, and the slope rises from the bottom at `-Z` to the top at `+Z`, where a vertical back face closes it. Slopes up to the slide angle (about 45 degrees: height not above the length along Z, see [`setSlideAngle`](#setslideangle)) can be walked on; steeper ones are slid down. Turn it with [`setRotation(double, double, double)`](#setrotation).

```js
// A ramp 4 blocks wide, rising 2 blocks over 4 blocks towards +Z
c.getWorld().createCollision("ramp").wedge(4, 2, 4).setPosition(0, 65, 4).spawn();
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sizeX` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | width, positive |
| `sizeY` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | height, positive |
| `sizeZ` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | length of the slope along Z, positive |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### sphere {#sphere}

::: member

Makes the collision a sphere with `#DEFAULT_SEGMENTS` meridians at once, see [`sphere(double, int)`](#sphere).

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `radius` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | radius, positive |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### sphere {#sphere-2}

::: member

Makes the collision a sphere at once, see [`setShape`](#setshape), built of flat faces between `segments`

meridians and `segments / 2` bands.

```js
c.getWorld().createCollision("ball").sphere(5, 24).setPosition(0, 70, 0).spawn();
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `radius` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | radius, positive |
| `segments` | [`int`](/scripting/js/Number) | number of meridians, from 4 to 32 |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### setShape {#setshape}

::: member

Gives the collision another shape at once, stopping a running [`transformTo`](#transformto) and [`sizeTo`](#sizeto). The shape is built around the anchor, so its position, rotation, anchor and material stay; the given sizes are its sizes in blocks, so an earlier [`setSize`](#setsize) is dropped. A new collision is a 1 x 1 x 1 box.

Shapes and their parameters, the same as of the methods named after them:

-  `"box"`: size X, size Y, size Z

-  `"cylinder"`: radius, height, optional number of sides (3 to 64, default `#DEFAULT_SEGMENTS`)

-  `"prism"`: polygon points `[x1, z1, x2, z2, ...]`, height

-  `"wedge"`: size X, size Y, size Z

-  `"sphere"`: radius, optional number of meridians (4 to 32, default `#DEFAULT_SEGMENTS`)

```js
c.getWorld().getCollision("pillar").setShape("cylinder", 1, 4);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `shape` | [`String`](/scripting/js/String) | shape name: `"box"`, `"cylinder"`, `"prism"`, `"wedge"` or `"sphere"` |
| `parameters` | `Any[]` | parameters of the shape, see above |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### transformTo {#transformto}

::: member

Smoothly turns the added collision into another shape over `durationTicks` ticks, replacing a running

`transformTo`; shapes and parameters are those of [`setShape`](#setshape), and the target keeps the position, rotation and anchor. On the way the collision stays a solid convex shape that entities collide with, standing entities are carried and others pushed out. A running [`sizeTo`](#sizeto) is stopped at its current size, and the target sizes are in blocks. A collision that is not added, or a duration of 0 or less, changes at once.

```js
var ball = c.getWorld().createCollision("ball").sphere(3).setPosition(0, 70, 0).spawn();

// The ball flattens into a disk 8 blocks wide in 2 seconds
ball.transformTo("sine_inout", 40, "cylinder", 4, 0.5, 24);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `interpolation` | [`String`](/scripting/js/String) | BBS interpolation name, e.g. `"linear"`; unknown names are linear |
| `durationTicks` | [`int`](/scripting/js/Number) | duration in ticks |
| `shape` | [`String`](/scripting/js/String) | target shape name, see [`setShape`](#setshape) |
| `parameters` | `Any[]` | parameters of the target shape, see [`setShape`](#setshape) |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### setAnchor {#setanchor}

::: member

Sets the anchor: the point that [`setPosition`](#setposition) places and that [`setRotation`](#setrotation) and [`setSize`](#setsize)

(and their animations) turn and resize around. The shape stays where it is; its position becomes the world position of the new anchor. The anchor is given in blocks from the center of the shape along its own axes at its current size, and keeps its spot on the shape when the shape is resized. By default it is the center. Stops a running [`moveTo`](#moveto), whose target was the position of the old anchor. Shown with hitboxes (F3 + B) as three axes: X red, Y green, Z blue.

```js
// A door 2 wide, 3 high, swinging open around its left edge
var door = c.getWorld().createCollision("door").box(2, 3, 0.25).setPosition(10, 65.5, 10).setAnchor(-1, 0, 0).spawn();

door.rotateTo("sine_out", 20, 0, 90, 0);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | blocks from the center along the shape's X |
| `y` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | blocks from the center along the shape's Y |
| `z` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | blocks from the center along the shape's Z |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### setAnchor {#setanchor-2}

::: member

Sets the anchor like [`setAnchor(double, double, double)`](#setanchor), either in blocks from the center or, when absolute, as fractions of the shape's bounds along its own axes: 0 is the minimum side, 0.5 the middle, 1 the maximum side. Values outside 0..1 place the anchor outside the shape. Either way the anchor keeps its spot on the shape when the shape is resized.

```js
// A door 2 wide, 3 high, standing on y = 65 with its left edge at x = 10, swinging open around that edge
var door = c.getWorld().createCollision("door").box(2, 3, 0.25).setAnchor(0, 0, 0.5, true).setPosition(10, 65, 10).spawn();

door.rotateTo("sine_out", 20, 0, 90, 0);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | blocks from the center along the shape's X, or the fraction of its bounds when absolute |
| `y` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | blocks from the center along the shape's Y, or the fraction of its bounds when absolute |
| `z` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | blocks from the center along the shape's Z, or the fraction of its bounds when absolute |
| `isAbsolute` | [`boolean`](/scripting/js/Boolean) | `true` for fractions of the bounds, `false` for blocks from the center |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### getAnchor {#getanchor}

::: member

**Returns** [`ScriptVector`](/scripting/common/ScriptVector) — anchor in blocks from the center of the shape along its own axes at its current size, see [`setAnchor`](#setanchor)

:::

### getAnchor {#getanchor-2}

::: member

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `isAbsolute` | [`boolean`](/scripting/js/Boolean) | `true` for fractions of the bounds, `false` for blocks from the center |

**Returns** [`ScriptVector`](/scripting/common/ScriptVector) — anchor as [`setAnchor(double, double, double, boolean)`](#setanchor) takes it: fractions of the shape's bounds along its own axes (0 minimum side, 1 maximum side) when absolute, otherwise as [`getAnchor()`](#getanchor)

:::

### getPosition {#getposition}

::: member

**Returns** [`ScriptVector`](/scripting/common/ScriptVector) — world position of the anchor, the center unless [`setAnchor`](#setanchor) moved it; during [`moveTo`](#moveto) the position of the current tick

:::

### setPosition {#setposition}

::: member

Moves the anchor (by default the center) of the shape at once, stopping a running [`moveTo`](#moveto).

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | world X |
| `y` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | world Y |
| `z` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | world Z |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### setPosition {#setposition-2}

::: member

Moves the anchor of the shape at once, see [`setPosition(double, double, double)`](#setposition).

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | [`ScriptVector`](/scripting/common/ScriptVector) | world position, not null |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### moveTo {#moveto}

::: member

Smoothly moves the anchor (by default the center) of the added shape to a world position over `durationTicks` ticks, replacing a running `moveTo`. A collision that is not added, or a duration of 0 or less, moves at once.

```js
// An elevator going up by 5 blocks in 3 seconds
var lift = c.getWorld().createCollision("lift").box(2, 0.5, 2).setPosition(0, 64.25, 0).spawn();

lift.moveTo("sine_inout", 60, 0, 69.25, 0);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `interpolation` | [`String`](/scripting/js/String) | BBS interpolation name, e.g. `"linear"`; unknown names are linear |
| `durationTicks` | [`int`](/scripting/js/Number) | duration in ticks |
| `x` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | target world X |
| `y` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | target world Y |
| `z` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | target world Z |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### setRotation {#setrotation}

::: member

Rotates the shape around its anchor (by default the center) at once, stopping a running [`rotateTo`](#rotateto): by roll around Z, then pitch around X, then yaw around Y. Angles follow the right-hand rule, so a positive yaw turns `+Z` towards `+X`.

```js
// A ramp rising towards +X instead of +Z
c.getWorld().createCollision("ramp").wedge(4, 2, 4).setPosition(0, 65, 0).setRotation(0, 90, 0).spawn();
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pitch` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | degrees around X |
| `yaw` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | degrees around Y |
| `roll` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | degrees around Z |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### rotateTo {#rotateto}

::: member

Smoothly rotates the added shape to the given angles over `durationTicks` ticks, replacing a running

`rotateTo`; angles are those of [`setRotation(double, double, double)`](#setrotation). Every angle goes from its current value straight to the target without wrapping, so a yaw from 0 to 720 makes two full turns. A collision that is not added, or a duration of 0 or less, rotates at once.

```js
// A platform spinning once around its center in 5 seconds
c.getWorld().getCollision("platform").rotateTo("linear", 100, 0, 360, 0);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `interpolation` | [`String`](/scripting/js/String) | BBS interpolation name, e.g. `"linear"`; unknown names are linear |
| `durationTicks` | [`int`](/scripting/js/Number) | duration in ticks |
| `pitch` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | target degrees around X |
| `yaw` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | target degrees around Y |
| `roll` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | target degrees around Z |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### getPitch {#getpitch}

::: member

**Returns** [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) — pitch in degrees, see [`setRotation(double, double, double)`](#setrotation)

:::

### getYaw {#getyaw}

::: member

**Returns** [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) — yaw in degrees, see [`setRotation(double, double, double)`](#setrotation)

:::

:::

### getSize {#getsize}

::: member

**Returns** [`ScriptVector`](/scripting/common/ScriptVector) — size of the shape along its own X, Y and Z before the rotation: for a box its sizes, for a cylinder or a sphere the diameter along X and Z and the height or diameter along Y

:::

### setSize {#setsize}

::: member

Resizes the shape at once, stopping a running [`sizeTo`](#sizeto). The shape is stretched along its own axes around its anchor, so with the default anchor a centered shape stays centered; sizes are those of [`getSize()`](#getsize).

```js
// A cylinder of radius 1 becomes radius 3, keeping its height of 2
c.getWorld().createCollision("pillar").cylinder(1, 2).setPosition(0, 65, 0).setSize(6, 2, 6).spawn();
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sizeX` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | size along the shape's X in blocks, positive |
| `sizeY` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | size along the shape's Y in blocks, positive |
| `sizeZ` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | size along the shape's Z in blocks, positive |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### sizeTo {#sizeto}

::: member

Smoothly resizes the added shape over `durationTicks` ticks, replacing a running `sizeTo`; sizes are those of [`setSize(double, double, double)`](#setsize), so a radius is changed through the diameter. A collision that is not added, or a duration of 0 or less, resizes at once.

```js
// A sphere of radius 2 grows to radius 4 in 2 seconds
c.getWorld().getCollision("bubble").sizeTo("sine_out", 40, 8, 8, 8);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `interpolation` | [`String`](/scripting/js/String) | BBS interpolation name, e.g. `"linear"`; unknown names are linear |
| `durationTicks` | [`int`](/scripting/js/Number) | duration in ticks |
| `sizeX` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | target size along the shape's X in blocks, positive |
| `sizeY` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | target size along the shape's Y in blocks, positive |
| `sizeZ` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | target size along the shape's Z in blocks, positive |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### setSneakEdges {#setsneakedges}

::: member

Sets whether sneaking players stop at the ledges of this collision, like at block edges. On by default; when off, sneaking players walk off this collision as if they were not sneaking.

```js
// A platform players can walk off even while sneaking
c.getWorld().createCollision("platform").box(3, 1, 3).setPosition(0, 65, 0).setSneakEdges(false).spawn();
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hasSneakEdges` | [`boolean`](/scripting/js/Boolean) | true to stop sneaking players at the ledges, false to let them walk off |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### hasSneakEdges {#hassneakedges}

::: member

**Returns** [`boolean`](/scripting/js/Boolean) — true if sneaking players stop at the ledges of this collision, see [`setSneakEdges(boolean)`](#setsneakedges)

:::

### setCarrying {#setcarrying}

::: member

Sets whether the collision moves entities when it moves, turns or resizes, like a shulker lid. On by default: entities standing on it move with it (along a turn too, without turning themselves), and entities in its way are pushed. When off, the collision moves alone: entities on it stay where they are, and entities it moves into can walk out of it.

```js
// A moving wall that does not push anyone
c.getWorld().createCollision("ghost_wall").box(4, 3, 0.5).setPosition(0, 65.5, 0).setCarrying(false).spawn().moveTo("linear", 100, 10, 65.5, 0);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `isCarrying` | [`boolean`](/scripting/js/Boolean) | true to carry and push entities, false to move without them |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### isCarrying {#iscarrying}

::: member

**Returns** [`boolean`](/scripting/js/Boolean) — true if the collision carries and pushes entities when it moves, see [`setCarrying(boolean)`](#setcarrying)

:::

### setSlipperiness {#setslipperiness}

::: member

Sets how slippery the top of the collision is, like the slipperiness of a block: entities walking on it speed up and stop more slowly the higher it is. Usual values, as of blocks: 0.6 (default, ordinary blocks), 0.8 (slime block), 0.98 (ice), 0.989 (blue ice). Other values work too: below 0.6 walking gets faster, as vanilla divides the walking speed by the cube of the slipperiness; above 1 entities on the collision speed up on their own.

```js
// An ice rink
c.getWorld().createCollision("rink").box(10, 0.5, 10).setPosition(0, 64.25, 0).setSlipperiness(0.98).spawn();
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `slipperiness` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | usually from 0.6 to 1, positive |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### getSlipperiness {#getslipperiness}

::: member

**Returns** [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) — slipperiness of the top of the collision, see [`setSlipperiness(double)`](#setslipperiness)

:::

### setStickiness {#setstickiness}

::: member

Sets how sticky the collision is, like a honey block at 1: entities standing on it walk slower (down to 0.4 of their speed) and jump lower (down to half), fall damage on it drops to a fifth, and entities falling along its sides slide down slowly. Usual values: 0 (default, not sticky) to 1 (honey); values between scale every effect. Other values work too: above 1 the effects grow further (walking stops at about 1.7 and turns back beyond), below 0 they turn around (faster walking, higher jumps).

```js
// A wall to slide down slowly
c.getWorld().createCollision("honey_wall").box(0.5, 10, 4).setPosition(0, 69, 0).setStickiness(1).spawn();
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stickiness` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | usually from 0 to 1 |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### getStickiness {#getstickiness}

::: member

**Returns** [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) — stickiness of the collision, see [`setStickiness(double)`](#setstickiness)

:::

### setBounciness {#setbounciness}

::: member

Sets how bouncy the collision is, like a slime block at 1: entities landing on it bounce back with that part of their landing speed and take that much less fall damage. On a slope they bounce away along its surface. Sneaking players do not bounce and take full damage, as on a slime block. Slow landings (resting, walking) do not bounce. Usual values: 0 (default, no bounce) to 1 (slime block, bounces back as high as fallen from); 0.5 bounces back with half the speed. Above 1 every bounce is higher than the last one (no fall damage then), 0 and below do not bounce.

```js
// A trampoline like a slime block
c.getWorld().createCollision("trampoline").cylinder(2, 0.5).setPosition(0, 64.25, 0).setBounciness(1).setSlipperiness(0.8).spawn();
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bounciness` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | usually from 0 to 1 |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### getBounciness {#getbounciness}

::: member

**Returns** [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) — bounciness of the collision, see [`setBounciness(double)`](#setbounciness)

:::

### setTranslucent {#settranslucent}

::: member

Sets whether players can target blocks through the collision. On by default, so the collision does not get in the way of the crosshair. When off, the crosshair stops at the collision like at a block: blocks and entities in and behind it cannot be selected, broken, used or attacked, and blocks cannot be placed into it (also checked by the server). To place blocks against the collision and use items on it, see [`setInteractive(boolean)`](#setinteractive).

```js
// A protected area: nobody can build or dig inside
c.getWorld().createCollision("vault").box(8, 5, 8).setPosition(0, 66.5, 0).setTranslucent(false).spawn();
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `isTranslucent` | [`boolean`](/scripting/js/Boolean) | true to let the crosshair through, false to stop it at the collision |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### isTranslucent {#istranslucent}

::: member

**Returns** [`boolean`](/scripting/js/Boolean) — true if players can target blocks through the collision, see [`setTranslucent(boolean)`](#settranslucent)

:::

### setInteractive {#setinteractive}

::: member

Sets whether players can interact with the collision like with a block: the crosshair stops at its surface (also when it is translucent), blocks can be placed against it, and items are used on it (buckets, spawn eggs, flint and steel...). Breaking does nothing, as there is no block to break. Off by default; blocks can never be placed into an interactive collision.

```js
// An invisible floor to build on
c.getWorld().createCollision("build_floor").box(16, 1, 16).setPosition(0, 99.5, 0).setInteractive(true).spawn();
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `isInteractive` | [`boolean`](/scripting/js/Boolean) | true to interact with the collision like with a block |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### isInteractive {#isinteractive}

::: member

**Returns** [`boolean`](/scripting/js/Boolean) — true if players can interact with the collision like with a block, see [`setInteractive(boolean)`](#setinteractive)

:::

### setSlideAngle {#setslideangle}

::: member

Sets the steepest slope of the collision entities can stand and walk on. Steeper surfaces are walls for walking, and entities slide down them in the air. Usual values: about 45.6 degrees (default, as for blocks), 0 (every slope but a flat top is slippery) up to about 85 (only near-vertical walls stop walking). From 90 on walls count as ground too, so entities could stand on them; negative angles work like positive ones.

```js
// A steep ramp players can still walk up
c.getWorld().createCollision("hill").wedge(4, 3, 3).setPosition(0, 65.5, 0).setSlideAngle(60).spawn();
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `degrees` | [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) | angle from the horizontal, usually from 0 to 85 |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### getSlideAngle {#getslideangle}

::: member

**Returns** [`double`](/scripting/js/Number) — steepest slope in degrees entities can stand on, see [`setSlideAngle(double)`](#setslideangle)

:::

### setClimbable {#setclimbable}

::: member

Sets whether entities can climb the sides of the collision like a ladder: walking into a side or jumping at it climbs up, falling along it is slow, sneaking players hold on, and climbing resets fall damage. Sliding wins: an entity touching a slope steeper than its slide angle (see [`setSlideAngle(double)`](#setslideangle)) slides down instead of climbing. Off by default.

```js
// A climbable pillar
c.getWorld().createCollision("pillar").cylinder(0.5, 8).setPosition(0, 68, 0).setClimbable(true).spawn();
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `isClimbable` | [`boolean`](/scripting/js/Boolean) | true to climb the sides, false for plain walls |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### isClimbable {#isclimbable}

::: member

**Returns** [`boolean`](/scripting/js/Boolean) — true if entities can climb the sides of the collision, see [`setClimbable(boolean)`](#setclimbable)

:::

### setDebugColor {#setdebugcolor}

::: member

Sets the color of the collision's edges in the hitbox debug view (F3 + B), to tell collisions apart.

```js
c.getWorld().getCollision("lift").setDebugColor(0xFF8800);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | [`long`](/scripting/js/Number) | `0xRRGGBB`; a higher byte (alpha) is ignored, the edges are always opaque |

**Returns** [`ScramServerCollision`](/scripting/server/ScramServerCollision) — this collision

:::

### getDebugColor {#getdebugcolor}

::: member

**Returns** [`int`](/scripting/js/Number) — `0xRRGGBB` of the edges in the hitbox debug view, see [`setDebugColor(long)`](#setdebugcolor)

:::
